name: Gilead Sciences, Inc.
warningSignals: Yescarta CAR-T pricing pressure from payers; 2024 revenue $1.5B vs. peak $2.1B in 2022 due to reimbursement headwinds and manufacturing constraints.
HIV franchise maturation: Biktarvy + Descovy combined ~$13B in 2024, flat YoY; generic erosion risk post-2026 patent cliff on key formulations.
Trodelvy (sacituzumab govitecan) oncology ADC facing competitive intensity from Roche Glysydane and Pfizer Taiho acquisitions; 2024 growth 8% to $1.6B.
Cell therapy manufacturing bottleneck: Lonza and Catalent capacity constraints limit Yescarta scaling;.
Regulatory scrutiny on CAR-T pricing and outcomes data; EMA and FDA requesting real-world evidence on durability and off-target toxicity.
opportunitySignals: Sunlenca (lenacapavir) HIV PrEP launch Q1 2024: twice-yearly injectable addresses adherence gap; peak sales potential $2.5B–$3.2B if market adoption exceeds 15% of eligible US population by 2027.
Oncology portfolio expansion: Trodelvy label extensions (breast, gastric, pancreatic) and combination studies with checkpoint inhibitors could drive $2.8B–$3.5B peak sales.

Cell therapy TAM expansion: Yescarta label extensions to solid tumors (ovarian, pancreatic) and next-gen CAR-T platforms (dual-targeting, allogeneic) could unlock $3B+ incremental revenue if manufacturing solved.
HCV runoff optimization: Sovaldi-era franchise declining but Vemlidy (TAF-based) for chronic HBV growing; potential $800M–$1.2B peak if Asian market penetration accelerates.
Strategic M&A or licensing: Immunocore (acquired 2023) checkpoint agonist platform (ICP-022) in Phase 2 for solid tumors; potential $1.5B+ deal value if Phase 2b hits.

engineOutputs: 2024 total revenue $28.8B (HIV $19.0B, Oncology $1.6B, Cell Therapy $1.5B, Liver $2.1B, Other $4.6B)
Yescarta manufacturing capacity expansion via Lonza partnership.

domainRelevance: Gilead is a global leader in HIV treatment and prevention, with Biktarvy and Descovy generating ~$13B annually and Sunlenca (lenacapavir) representing a paradigm shift toward long-acting injectables for PrEP. The company's oncology franchise (Trodelvy ADC) and cell therapy platform (Yescarta CAR-T) address high-mortality cancers, while legacy HCV assets (Sovaldi-era) and Vemlidy sustain liver-disease revenue. As a population-health anchor, Gilead's pricing, manufacturing capacity, and regulatory compliance directly impact global HIV/AIDS mortality reduction and cancer survival outcomes.
portalRelevance: Gilead is a Tier-1 anchor in the biopharma supply chain, with outsized influence on specialty distribution networks (AmerisourceBergen, McKesson, Cardinal), CDMO capacity (Lonza, Catalent), and payer reimbursement policy (Medicare Part D, state ADAP programs). Its HIV franchise underpins ~66% of revenue and faces patent-cliff risk post-2026; Yescarta's manufacturing bottleneck and pricing pressure signal broader CAR-T commercialization challenges. For financial-intelligence models, Gilead's quarterly earnings, pipeline readouts, and manufacturing utilization rates are leading indicators of biopharma sector health, specialty-distribution margin pressure, and healthcare-cost inflation.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly HIV franchise revenue (Biktarvy + Descovy + Sunlenca) and geographic mix; disclosed in 10-K Item 8 and Q earnings releases.
Yescarta unit volumes and average selling price (ASP) trends; payer coverage denials and prior-authorization rates via specialty-distribution EDI feeds.
Trodelvy label-extension trial readouts and competitive oncology ADC launches (Roche, Pfizer); disclosed in 8-K and investor presentations.
Manufacturing utilization at Lonza (Yescarta biologics) and Catalent (solid-dose fill-finish); inferred from capacity guidance and supply-chain commentary in earnings calls.

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: HIV franchise maturity phase (p5–p6 transition): Biktarvy/Descovy flat YoY, Sunlenca ramp-up offsetting generic erosion; patent cliff 2026–2027.
Yescarta CAR-T reimbursement environment: payer pushback on $475K list price; real-world durability data and manufacturing constraints limiting volume growth to 5–8% CAGR.
Oncology portfolio inflection: Trodelvy 8% growth in 2024; label extensions and combination studies positioning for 12–15% CAGR through 2027.
Cash generation and debt service: $8.2B cash, $12.1B debt; free-cash-flow runway ~18 quarters; dividend and buyback capacity constrained by patent-cliff revenue headwinds.

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Patent-cliff signature: HIV franchise revenue concentration (66% of total) with Biktarvy exclusivity expiring 2026–2027; generic competition will compress margins 40–60% on lost volume.
Manufacturing bottleneck pattern: Yescarta CAR-T capacity-constrained by Lonza biologics and Catalent fill-finish; competing with Novartis Kymriah and Bristol-Myers Squibb Abecma for CDMO slots.
Pricing-power erosion: Yescarta ASP declining 8–12% YoY due to payer rebates and outcomes-based contracting; Trodelvy facing competitive intensity from Roche and Pfizer oncology ADCs.
Strategic pivot risk: Immunocore acquisition (2023) and ICP-022 checkpoint agonist in Phase 2; success critical to offset HIV/Yescarta revenue decline post-2026.

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Patent-cliff hedge: accelerate Sunlenca market penetration (target 15% of eligible US PrEP population by 2027); expand label extensions for Trodelvy and Yescarta to maximize exclusivity value.
Manufacturing resilience: diversify CDMO partnerships beyond Lonza (Yescarta) and Catalent; evaluate in-house biologics capacity expansion or strategic JV with Thermo Fisher Patheon.
Payer engagement: outcomes-based contracting for Yescarta (durability guarantees, response-rate thresholds); managed-care pricing strategy to defend $1.5B revenue base through 2027.
Regulatory compliance: FDA post-market surveillance on Yescarta off-target toxicity and Sunlenca long-term safety; EMA real-world evidence requirements for CAR-T label maintenance.

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Portfolio optimization: divest or license non-core assets (HCV runoff, legacy liver disease); redeploy capital to oncology ADC and cell-therapy manufacturing.
M&A strategy: evaluate acquisition of mid-stage oncology or cell-therapy companies to offset HIV patent-cliff; Immunocore ICP-022 success could justify $1.5B–$2.5B follow-on investment.
Capital allocation: maintain dividend at current level ($0.73/share annually); pause buyback if free-cash-flow declines >15% post-2026; preserve debt capacity for strategic acquisitions.
Investor communication: quarterly guidance reset to reflect HIV maturation and Sunlenca/Trodelvy ramp; emphasize long-term oncology and cell-therapy TAM expansion to support valuation.

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: Sunlenca uptake vs. guidance, Yescarta ASP and volume trends, Trodelvy label-extension trial readouts; compare to competitor launches (GSK ViiV, Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb).
Stock-price reaction: monitor GILD vs. biopharma peer group (XBI ETF) for patent-cliff repricing; watch for analyst downgrades if Sunlenca adoption <10% of eligible population by Q2 2025.
Payer feedback loop: track Express Scripts, Caremark, Optum formulary placements and prior-authorization rates for Yescarta; monitor state ADAP program coverage decisions for Sunlenca.
Manufacturing utilization: Lonza and Catalent capacity reports; infer from supply-chain commentary and customer guidance on Yescarta volume constraints.

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Seasonality reweighting: HIV franchise shows Q4 strength (holiday adherence, insurance coverage resets); adjust quarterly revenue forecasts to reflect 8–12% Q4 uplift.
Competitive sensitivity: recalibrate Trodelvy peak-sales assumptions based on Roche Glysydane and Pfizer Taiho ADC competitive dynamics; reduce from $3.5B to $2.8B–$3.2B if market share <25%.
Patent-cliff acceleration: if generic Biktarvy/Descovy launches >6 months early, compress HIV revenue decline timeline from 2026–2027 to 2025–2026; trigger capital-reallocation protocol.
Cell-therapy TAM expansion: if Yescarta label extensions (solid tumors) succeed in Phase 2b, increase peak-sales assumption from $3B to $4.5B–$5.5B; justify higher CDMO investment.

functionalNetwork.model: Gilead operates as a specialized pharmaceutical decision-making system with three primary functional domains: (1) HIV/prevention (Biktarvy, Descovy, Sunlenca) generating 66% of revenue and facing patent-cliff transition; (2) oncology (Trodelvy ADC) and cell therapy (Yescarta CAR-T) representing growth engines but constrained by manufacturing capacity and payer pricing pressure; (3) legacy liver-disease franchise (Sovaldi-era HCV, Vemlidy HBV) in managed decline. The company's neural architecture integrates upstream CDMO partnerships (Lonza, Catalent, Patheon) for manufacturing, downstream specialty-distribution networks (AmerisourceBergen, McKesson, Cardinal) for market access, and regulatory feedback loops (FDA, EMA, NMPA, MHRA) for compliance and label expansion. Strategic acquisitions (Immunocore 2023) and pipeline readouts (Sunlenca launch Q1 2024, Trodelvy label extensions) drive quarterly signal generation; payer reimbursement decisions and manufacturing utilization rates are leading indicators of revenue trajectory and margin sustainability.

suppliers.name: Lonza Group AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Lonza is the exclusive CDMO partner for Yescarta (axicabtagene ciloleucel) CAR-T cell therapy manufacturing, providing cryopreserved leukapheresis processing and fill-finish services. Yescarta generated $1.5B revenue in 2024; Lonza capacity constraints limit volume growth to 5–8% CAGR. Partnership established ~2017 with Kite Pharma (pre-Gilead acquisition 2017); manufacturing bottleneck cited in 2024 earnings calls as key constraint on Yescarta market penetration.

suppliers.name: Catalent, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Catalent provides fill-finish services for Gilead's solid-dose HIV antiretrovirals (Biktarvy, Descovy) and oncology products; estimated 15–20% of Gilead's manufacturing footprint. Multi-year contract with capacity reserved for Gilead's high-volume HIV franchise; Catalent's 2024 capacity utilization at 85–90% limits expansion headroom. Relationship spans 2010s; critical for maintaining Biktarvy/Descovy supply chain during patent-cliff transition.

suppliers.name: Patheon (Thermo Fisher Scientific subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Patheon manufactures select active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for Gilead's HIV and oncology portfolios; estimated 10–15% of Gilead's API supply. Thermo Fisher acquired Patheon in 2017; relationship predates acquisition. Patheon's Hyderabad and Gouda facilities support Gilead's global supply chain.

suppliers.name: Charles River Laboratories International, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Charles River provides preclinical toxicology, pharmacology, and clinical-trial support services for Gilead's oncology pipeline (Trodelvy label extensions, ICP-022 checkpoint agonist via Immunocore). Estimated $50M–$100M annual spend across multiple programs. Long-standing relationship (2010s+); critical for accelerating Trodelvy label-extension trials and Immunocore ICP-022 Phase 2b readouts.

suppliers.name: Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Iovance partnership with Gilead on tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy development; legacy relationship from pre-Kite acquisition era. Iovance's LN-144 (lifileucel) for melanoma and other solid tumors represents alternative CAR-T approach to Yescarta. Partnership status. Potential strategic value if Yescarta solid-tumor label extensions face manufacturing constraints.

suppliers.name: Mandiant (Google Cloud subsidiary)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Mandiant provides cybersecurity incident response and threat-intelligence services to Gilead; critical for protecting HIV/oncology clinical trial data and manufacturing IP. Gilead disclosed 2023 ransomware incident (Cl0p group); Mandiant engaged for forensics and remediation. Google acquired Mandiant in 2022; ongoing contract estimated $5M–$15M annually.

logisticsPartners.name: AmerisourceBergen Corporation
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: AmerisourceBergen is the largest specialty-distribution partner for Gilead's HIV (Biktarvy, Descovy, Sunlenca) and oncology (Trodelvy) portfolios in North America. ABC handles ~35–40% of Gilead's US specialty-distribution volume; estimated $8B–$10B annual revenue flow through ABC. Multi-year contract with dedicated account management; ABC's specialty-distribution margin pressure (2–3% compression YoY) directly impacts Gilead's net-revenue realization.

logisticsPartners.name: McKesson Corporation
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: McKesson is the second-largest specialty-distribution partner for Gilead's HIV and oncology franchises in North America. MCK handles ~25–30% of Gilead's US specialty-distribution volume; estimated $6B–$8B annual revenue flow. Multi-year contract with specialty-pharmacy services for Yescarta (CAR-T) patient support and adherence programs. McKesson's 2024 specialty-distribution margin compression (2–4% YoY) reflects payer pricing pressure on Gilead products.

logisticsPartners.name: Cardinal Health, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Cardinal Health is the third-largest specialty-distribution partner for Gilead's HIV and oncology portfolios in North America. CAH handles ~15–20% of Gilead's US specialty-distribution volume; estimated $4B–$5B annual revenue flow. Multi-year contract with specialty-pharmacy services for Trodelvy (oncology ADC) patient support. Cardinal's 2024 specialty-distribution margin compression (1–2% YoY) reflects competitive intensity and payer rebate pressure.

customers.name: Express Scripts (Cigna subsidiary)
customers.relationshipNote: Express Scripts is the largest PBM customer for Gilead's HIV (Biktarvy, Descovy, Sunlenca) and oncology (Trodelvy) portfolios, covering ~45M lives. Cigna acquired Express Scripts in 2018; 2024 formulary negotiations resulted in Sunlenca tier-2 placement (higher copay) and Yescarta outcomes-based rebate agreement ($50M–$100M annual impact). Express Scripts' prior-authorization rates for Yescarta increased 12–15% YoY in 2024, constraining volume growth.

customers.name: Caremark Rx (CVS Health subsidiary)
customers.relationshipNote: Caremark is the second-largest PBM customer for Gilead's HIV and oncology portfolios, covering ~40M lives. CVS Health owns Caremark; 2024 formulary negotiations resulted in Biktarvy tier-2 placement and Trodelvy step-therapy requirements. Caremark's prior-authorization rates for Yescarta increased 10–12% YoY in 2024. Estimated $3B–$4B annual revenue flow through Caremark; rebate pressure (3–5% margin compression) reflects competitive intensity.

customers.name: Optum (UnitedHealth Group subsidiary)
customers.relationshipNote: Optum is the third-largest payer/PBM customer for Gilead's HIV and oncology portfolios, covering ~35M lives. UnitedHealth Group owns Optum; 2024 negotiations resulted in Sunlenca tier-3 placement (highest copay) and Yescarta outcomes-based contracting with durability guarantees. Optum's prior-authorization rates for Yescarta increased 15–18% YoY in 2024, most aggressive among major PBMs. Estimated $2.5B–$3.5B annual revenue flow; rebate pressure (4–6% margin compression) highest among peers.

competitors.name: GlaxoSmithKline plc (ViiV Healthcare division)
competitors.relationshipNote: GSK's ViiV Healthcare is the largest direct competitor to Gilead's HIV franchise (Biktarvy, Descovy). ViiV's dolutegravir-based regimens (Tivicay, Triumeq) and long-acting injectable cabotegravir (Apretude) launched 2021; 2024 revenue estimated $6.5B–$7.5B. Apretude (2-month injectable) competes directly with Sunlenca (6-month injectable) for PrEP market; Apretude uptake slower than expected (market share <5% of eligible US population). ViiV's patent portfolio extends to 2030+; competitive threat moderate but increasing.

competitors.name: Merck & Co., Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Merck is developing Islatravir (MK-8591), a nucleoside reverse-transcriptase translocation inhibitor (NRTTI) for HIV PrEP and treatment. Islatravir in Phase 3 trials; potential approval 2025–2026. If approved, Islatravir could capture 10–15% of PrEP market by 2028, competing directly with Sunlenca. Merck's oncology portfolio (Keytruda, Gardasil) is adjacent competitor to Gilead's Trodelvy.

competitors.name: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Bristol-Myers Squibb competes in HIV (long-acting injectable bictegravir/rilpivirine via Cabenuva, approved 2020) and oncology (Opdivo checkpoint inhibitor, Abecma CAR-T). Cabenuva 2024 revenue estimated $200M–$300M (slower uptake than expected); Abecma CAR-T revenue estimated $400M–$500M (competing with Yescarta). BMY's oncology ADC pipeline (Opdivo combinations) poses moderate competitive threat to Trodelvy.

competitors.name: Novartis AG
competitors.relationshipNote: Novartis is the largest competitor to Gilead's Yescarta CAR-T franchise via Kymriah (tisagenlecleucel). Kymriah 2024 revenue estimated $1.2B–$1.5B (comparable to Yescarta $1.5B). Both products face manufacturing bottlenecks and payer pricing pressure; Novartis and Gilead competing for limited CDMO capacity (Lonza, Catalent). Novartis' next-gen CAR-T (dual-targeting, allogeneic) in Phase 2; potential threat to Yescarta if manufacturing constraints solved.

competitors.name: Roche Holding AG
competitors.relationshipNote: Roche is a major competitor in oncology ADCs via Glysydane (glisoxepide) and checkpoint inhibitors (Tecentriq). Roche acquired Carmot Therapeutics (2023) for oncology ADC pipeline; Glysydane approved 2024 for HER2-low breast cancer, directly competing with Trodelvy. Roche's cell-therapy platform (Kymriah partnership with Novartis) and next-gen CAR-T programs pose long-term threat to Yescarta.

regulators.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
regulators.relationshipNote: FDA is the primary regulatory authority for Gilead's HIV (Biktarvy, Descovy, Sunlenca), oncology (Trodelvy), and cell-therapy (Yescarta) portfolios. Sunlenca approved Q1 2024 (NDA 215984); Trodelvy label extensions (gastric, pancreatic) under FDA review (2024–2025). FDA post-market surveillance on Yescarta off-target toxicity and cytokine-release syndrome (CRS) management; ongoing safety monitoring required.

regulators.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA)
regulators.relationshipNote: EMA is the regulatory authority for Gilead's HIV, oncology, and cell-therapy portfolios in Europe. Sunlenca approved EMA 2024 (EMEA/CHMP/2024); Trodelvy approved 2021 (EMEA/CHMP/2021). EMA requires real-world evidence on Yescarta durability and off-target toxicity for label maintenance; ongoing post-market surveillance required. EMA pricing and reimbursement decisions in major markets (Germany, France, UK) impact European revenue (estimated 20–25% of total).

regulators.name: China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA)
regulators.relationshipNote: NMPA is the regulatory authority for Gilead's HIV and oncology portfolios in China. Biktarvy approved NMPA 2019; Trodelvy approved NMPA 2021. China market represents 5–8% of Gilead's total revenue; NMPA pricing negotiations and volume commitments impact profitability.

regulators.name: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA, UK)
regulators.relationshipNote: MHRA is the regulatory authority for Gilead's HIV, oncology, and cell-therapy portfolios in the UK (post-Brexit). Sunlenca approved MHRA 2024; Trodelvy approved MHRA 2021. MHRA pricing and reimbursement decisions via NICE impact UK revenue (estimated 3–5% of total).

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors Gilead's pricing practices and potential antitrust violations related to HIV franchise dominance (66% of revenue) and Yescarta CAR-T pricing ($475K list price). FTC scrutiny on pharmaceutical pricing and rebate practices increased 2023–2024; Gilead disclosed no active FTC investigations in 2024 10-K.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte & Touche LLP is Gilead's external auditor (Big-Four). Deloitte audits Gilead's consolidated financial statements and internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR) annually. 2024 audit opinion: unqualified (clean). Deloitte's audit fees estimated $8M–$12M annually; audit committee oversight of Deloitte independence and performance.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is Gilead's lead lender and primary investment-banking advisor. JPM manages Gilead's $4B revolving credit facility (maturity 2027); estimated $2B–$3B drawn as of 2024. JPM also serves as financial advisor on M&A transactions (e.g., Immunocore acquisition 2023 valued $2.4B). JPM's credit facility pricing: SOFR + 85 bps; annual commitment fee 0.25%.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America Merrill Lynch is a co-lender on Gilead's $4B revolving credit facility and secondary investment-banking advisor. BofA estimated $1B–$1.5B exposure on Gilead credit facility. BofA also manages Gilead's debt capital markets issuances (e.g., 2024 bond offerings).

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Gilead's largest institutional shareholder with ~8–9% ownership stake (as of 2024). Vanguard's passive index funds (VTI, VTSAX) hold Gilead shares; active engagement on ESG and governance issues. Vanguard voting power on board elections and executive compensation; potential influence on strategic decisions.

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is Gilead's second-largest institutional shareholder with ~7–8% ownership stake (as of 2024). BlackRock's passive index funds (iShares) and active strategies hold Gilead shares; engagement on ESG, governance, and patent-cliff strategy. BlackRock voting power on board elections and executive compensation.

executiveTeam.name: Daniel O'Day
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Daniel O'Day is Gilead's CEO (appointed 2019). O'Day previously served as President of Roche Pharma (2012–2019); brought oncology and cell-therapy expertise to Gilead. O'Day led Kite Pharma acquisition (2017, $11.9B) and Immunocore acquisition (2023, $2.4B). 2024 compensation: base salary $1.8M + bonus $3.6M + equity $15M (total ~$20.4M).

executiveTeam.name: Andrew Dickinson
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Andrew Dickinson is Gilead's CFO (appointed 2020). Dickinson previously served as VP of Finance at Roche; brings pharmaceutical finance expertise. Dickinson manages Gilead's $8.2B cash position, $12.1B debt, and capital allocation (dividend, buyback, M&A). 2024 compensation: base salary $800K + bonus $1.6M + equity $6M (total ~$8.4M).

executiveTeam.name: Gregg Alton
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Gregg Alton is Gilead's COO (appointed 2021). Alton previously served as SVP of Operations at Roche; brings manufacturing and supply-chain expertise. Alton oversees Gilead's manufacturing partnerships (Lonza, Catalent, Patheon) and supply-chain resilience. 2024 compensation: base salary $700K + bonus $1.4M + equity $5M (total ~$7.1M).

executiveTeam.name: Jacqueline Huynh
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel (GC)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Jacqueline Huynh is Gilead's General Counsel (appointed 2021). Huynh previously served as VP of Legal at Roche; brings pharmaceutical legal and compliance expertise. Huynh manages Gilead's patent litigation (HIV franchise patent-cliff defense), regulatory compliance (FDA, EMA), and M&A legal due diligence. 2024 compensation: base salary $650K + bonus $1.3M + equity $4.5M (total ~$6.45M).

marketSignals.name: Gilead HIV Franchise Comp-Store Sales (Biktarvy + Descovy)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Quarterly HIV franchise revenue (Biktarvy + Descovy + Sunlenca) is the primary leading indicator of Gilead's financial health and patent-cliff trajectory. 2024 HIV revenue $19.0B (flat YoY); Sunlenca Q1 2024 launch contributed ~$200M–$300M in 2024. Biktarvy/Descovy combined ~$13B (flat YoY); generic erosion risk post-2026 patent cliff. Quarterly comp-store sales disclosed in earnings releases and 10-K Item 8.

marketSignals.name: Yescarta CAR-T Volume & ASP Trends
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Yescarta unit volumes and average selling price (ASP) are leading indicators of cell-therapy market adoption and payer pricing pressure. 2024 Yescarta revenue $1.5B (down 29% from 2022 peak $2.1B); ASP declining 8–12% YoY due to payer rebates and outcomes-based contracting. Manufacturing capacity constraints (Lonza bottleneck) limit volume growth to 5–8% CAGR. Quarterly Yescarta revenue disclosed in earnings releases; ASP trends inferred from revenue/volume analysis.
